metaData.originalTitle: A Three-Phase Factual Recall Circuit in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT
metaData.title: A Three-Phase Factual Recall Circuit in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This paper presents a mechanistic interpretability study localizing a three-phase factual recall circuit (storage, routing, readout) in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT via activation patching, with the circuit scaling proportionally across model sizes.
metaData.summary: The author designs a battery of 60 clean/corrupt prompt pairs across 20 fact categories and uses activation patching with TransformerLens to isolate factual recall circuits in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT. A novel metric called TotalSwing is introduced to rank prompt pairs by signal strength. Four experiments progressively narrow down from full residual stream to individual attention heads. Results reveal a consistent three-phase circuit: (1) Storage in the residual stream at the entity token position (layers 0-14 in 2B, 0-27 in 12B), (2) Distributed routing via attention heads (no single dominant head), and (3) Readout as a pass-through in the final layers (layers 15-17 in 2B, proportionally in 12B). The circuit replicates at scale, but tokenizer differences cause dataset drift between models, a caveat for cross-model comparisons. The author discusses future work including path patching and SAE analysis, constrained by disk space limitations. The full codebase is open-sourced.

mainPoints.point: Factual recall in Gemma follows a three-phase circuit: storage, routing, and readout.
mainPoints.explanation: Storage happens in the residual stream at the entity token's position (layers 0–14 for 2B, 0–27 for 12B). Routing is distributed across attention heads with no single dominant head. Readout is a simple pass-through in the final layers.

mainPoints.point: The residual stream dominates causal effect over individual sublayers in the storage phase.
mainPoints.explanation: In Gemma-2B, residual stream damage (ΔLD = -11.47) is 18x larger than MLP output damage and 40x larger than attention output damage, confirming facts are encoded as directions in the stream.

mainPoints.point: The three-phase circuit replicates at scale from 2B to 12B parameters.
mainPoints.explanation: Gemma-12B-IT shows the same structure proportionally: storage shifts to layers 0–27, routing remains distributed and even duller, and readout concentrates in the final layers.

mainPoints.point: Tokenizer differences introduce dataset drift that constrains cross-model comparisons.
mainPoints.explanation: Even models sharing the same tokenizer (SentencePiece) can map some words to different token IDs (e.g., 'hertz' as two tokens), causing prompt pair exclusion in larger models and requiring upfront token run checks.

keyQuotes: there exists a three-phase factual recall circuit within the Gemma model family
Facts are encoded as directions in the residual stream at the entity token. The residual stream dominates causally here, contributing 40× more than attention outputs and 18× more than MLP outputs.

I found that this three-phase circuit replicated at scale: storage shifted to layers 0–27, routing remained distributed with no significantly dominant head, and readout concentrated in the final layers, structurally identical to Gemma-2B, proportionally scaled
cross-model mechanistic comparisons are partly constrained by tokenizer-induced dataset drift, and reported differences should be interpreted with that caveat in mind

relatedArticles.title: Hybrid Search and Re-Ranking in Production RAG
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a production-grade approach to improving RAG retrieval quality by combining hybrid search (BM25 + dense vectors) with cross-encoder re-ranking and metadata filtering, supported by real-world evaluation metrics.

relatedArticles.title: Building an Evaluation Harness for Production AI Agents: A 12-Metric Framework From 100+ Deployments
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a comprehensive 12-metric evaluation framework for production AI agents, distilled from over 100 enterprise deployments, covering retrieval, generation, agent behavior, and production health.

relatedArticles.title: Stop Treating AI Memory Like a Search Problem
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article critiques the conventional 'store-and-retrieve' approach to AI memory, proposing a lifecycle-based system with decay, contradiction detection, confidence scoring, compression, and expiry to manage memory like a human brain rather than a static archive.

relatedArticles.title: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code  | Claude
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Claude Code's dynamic workflows let Claude write custom agentic harnesses on the fly, enabling it to tackle complex, multi-step tasks that a single context window cannot handle reliably.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5, a generally available Mythos-class model with state-of-the-art capabilities, alongside Claude Mythos 5 for trusted cybersecurity partners, with new safeguards to mitigate misuse risks.

relatedArticles.title: Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces a major upgrade to ChatGPT's memory system, using a more scalable 'dreaming' architecture that automatically synthesizes memories from chat history to improve freshness, continuity, and relevance.

relatedArticles.title: Your ReAct Agent Is Wasting 90% of Its Retries — Here’s How to Stop It
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article identifies a critical architectural flaw in ReAct-style LLM agents where hallucinated tool names waste the majority of retry budgets, and proposes three structural fixes—error taxonomy, per-tool circuit breakers, and deterministic tool routing—to eliminate this waste and improve production reliability.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces GPT-5.5, a new category of AI that acts as an autonomous agent capable of planning, reasoning, and executing complex multi-step tasks across different applications.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: Embeddings Aren’t Magic: The Predictable Failure Modes of RAG Retrieval
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically debunks the magic of embeddings in RAG systems, demonstrating through reproducible experiments that embeddings excel at public vocabulary tasks but predictably fail on enterprise-specific terms, negation, magnitudes, and answer relevance, advocating for upstream filtering over stronger models.
